title.value: Collegiality as political work: Professions in today’s world of organizations
title.justification: The paper discusses the political aspect of collegiality within professions, arguing its dynamic role in organizational governance.
title.quote: Collegiality as political work: Professions in today’s world of organizations.

analysis.description: This paper examines the concept of collegiality within professional work, arguing that it is not a static characteristic but a result of political work by professionals to balance organizational and professional principles in a modern context.

type.justification: The paper presents a theoretical analysis of collegiality within professional organizations, drawing on various sociological and organizational theories.
type.quote: It is conceived and developed in the form of a theoretical essay where we analyse scholarly works relevant to understanding the work of professions in contemporary societies and organizations.

name.justification: The research focuses on the interaction of professional collegiality and organizational governance, a topic central to the Sociology of Professions.
name.quote: Sociological work on professions has attempted to define a set of core attributes or traits that distinguish professions from other work roles or occupational categories.

name.justification: The paper explores the role of collegiality in organizational contexts, considering its impact on governance.
name.quote: Our arguments build on recent studies and hypotheses concerning the interface of professions and organizations to reveal the political work that underlies the affirmation and re-affirmation of collegiality as a mode of governance.

name.justification: Health care is mentioned as a domain where the dynamics of collegiality are particularly relevant, impacting professional governance.
name.quote: Illustrations of situations of resistance and co-production in professionalized organizations: The case of healthcare.
